gap: No result ChatGPT got works out what each station's own solar kit does while the AC is running. Take a 5,000 BTU window AC at its rated CEER of 11 (about 455 W while cooling). The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit ($1,499) has 400 W of panels. In full sun those panels cover more than the AC's average draw at 50% duty (268 W from the battery), so the battery still gains about 132 W. With the compressor on all the time, the battery loses 135 W, which stretches a full charge to about 15 hours instead of 3.9. None of these results gives cost per usable Wh either.
standout_why: Pages compared: BuyerSheet (cited), GeneratorChecker (cited), StationHours window AC, and ChatGPT's answer. BuyerSheet gives runtimes for an 8,000 BTU unit at 60% duty only, with no solar math and no cost per Wh. GeneratorChecker derives the draw from CEER, but only for 8,000 BTU units, and its only solar example is the DELTA 2 Max with 400 W of panels (about 4.6 h); it has no kit prices and no cost per Wh. StationHours gives refill time at each station's maximum solar input, not from the panel that actually ships in a bundle, and works out no net drain while the AC runs and no cost. ChatGPT's answer has a runtime table but no solar figures and no cost per usable Wh.
decides: This supports the 2 kWh class (Elite 200 V2 or C2000 Gen 2) as the value pick when the shopper adds a 400 W solar kit. With a 5,000 BTU AC running half the time, the 400 W kit keeps the Elite 200 V2 charging during full sun, so daytime cooling has no hard limit and the battery is left for the evening (about 7.7 h at 50% duty). Without panels, neither 2 kWh unit gets a 5,000 BTU AC through a full 8-hour night even at 50% duty: the Elite 200 V2 gets about 7.7 h and the C2000 Gen 2 about 7.65 h. That is the case for a 3 kWh station (Elite 300 or DELTA 3 Ultra), but I did not source those two this session.

findings.label: 5,000 BTU window AC average draw while cooling (Frigidaire FFRA051WAE)
findings.source_title: Frigidaire 5,000 BTU 115 V White Window-Mounted Room Air Conditioner - FFRA051WAE (Abt)
findings.note: The listing gives Cooling BTU 5000, CEER 11, 115 V. W = BTU/h ÷ CEER = 5000 ÷ 11 = 455 W. CEER includes standby power, so the figure is approximate. A search snippet put the maker's spec sheet at 450 W, but the PDF would not render, so I did not use that number.

findings.label: Runtime assumptions used below
findings.value: 85% of rated Wh usable; duty cycle stated per figure (100% or 50%)
findings.source_title: Best Power Station for a Window AC (5,000 BTU): 30 Models Compared | StationHours
findings.note: StationHours assumes 85% usable energy, inverter losses included, and plans for 60–80% duty on hot days. I use 85% so my figures are directly comparable with StationHours and ChatGPT. The 50% figure is a stated assumption, not a measurement.

findings.label: Full-sun net battery flow while the AC runs, 2×200 W kit
findings.value: +132 W at 50% duty (gaining charge); −135 W with the compressor always on (about 15.4 h from full)

findings.note: Battery-side AC draw = 455 ÷ 0.85 = 535 W (always on) or 268 W (50% duty). 400 W rated panels − 268 W = +132 W. 535 − 400 = −135 W, and 2,073.6 Wh ÷ 135 W = 15.4 h. Assumes panels give their full rated 400 W, which is best case; real output is lower.

findings.note: 2,073.6 Wh ÷ 400 W = 5.2 h; 2,073.6 Wh ÷ 200 W = 10.4 h. Best case at full rated panel output. BLUETTI states no solar charge time.

BLUETTI Elite 300, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra and Anker SOLIX F3800 runtimes and prices: the BLUETTI Elite 300 page hit too many redirects, and I ran out of calls before the other two. These are the 3 kWh+ candidates that would cover a full 8-hour night at 50% duty.
